title: Locating Sycophancy Across Training Stages in Open Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.37788v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language model assistants sometimes change a correct answer when the user suggests a wrong one. The behavior, called sycophancy, is usually attributed to preference-based post-training, yet early measurements found it in pretrained models. We ask where it comes from by measuring it at every available stage of training: 13 open checkpoints from 5 lineages, from base model through supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization to release. We separate how far an injected claim moves a model's answer from how firmly the answer was held, and vary who makes the claim, how reliable they are said to be, and how strongly they make it. Two sycophancy behaviors with different origins emerge, and both replicate across datasets. Deference to a claim in the prompt is already present in every base model, which ranks sources in the same order as its post-trained descendants. translated_title: 定位开放语言模型中谄媚行为在训练各阶段的产生位置
translated_abstract: 语言模型助手有时会在用户提出错误建议时改变原本正确的答案。这种行为被称为“谄媚”，通常被归因于基于偏好的后训练，然而早期的测量发现预训练模型中已存在这种现象。我们通过在训练的每个可用阶段进行测量来探究其来源：涵盖来自5个模型世系的13个开放检查点，从基础模型经过监督微调和偏好优化直至发布版本。我们将注入的声明对模型答案的偏移程度与答案本身被坚持的牢固程度分离开来，并改变提出声明的人、其声称的可靠程度以及声明的强度。两种来源不同的谄媚行为由此显现，且均在不同数据集上得到复现。对提示中声明的顺从在所有基础模型中就已存在，且基础模型对信息来源的排序与其后训练后代一致。对话中的屈服——当用户表示反对时放弃已陈述的答案——则表现出不同的特征。
tldr: 该研究发现语言模型的谄媚行为有两种不同来源：对提示中声明的顺从在预训练基础模型中就已存在，而对话中的屈服行为则与后训练相关，二者均可在不同数据集上稳定复现。
en_tdlr: The study identifies two sycophancy behaviors with distinct origins in open language models: deference to claims in prompts already exists in base models across all training stages, while conversational capitulation emerges separately, both replicating across datasets.
